notes: Correlation between forecast and realized return was negative across nearly all instruments/horizons. RESOLVED via Monte Carlo simulation (300 sims, pure i.i.d. random walk): confirmed this is a known structural artifact of overlapping-window trailing-mean estimators (mean correlation -0.02 to -0.06, growing more negative with horizon, even under zero true autocorrelation) - not a real market finding. Embargo added to the evaluation split (see backtest_engine/splitting.py) as a separate, unrelated methodology improvement.
decision: Does not clear the bar to build on. RMSE beats naive-zero in only ~20% of instrument-horizon combinations; sign agreement is near coin-flip on average and inconsistent across asset classes (near-zero on FX, mildly positive on indices/metals, negative on crypto). Treated as the expected null-hypothesis result, not a failure.
influenced_later_decisions: Establishes the baseline Model 2 (time-series) must beat out of sample, after costs, to be added.

notes: Ablation test against Model 1 on identical out-of-sample rows, embargo-adjusted split.
decision: Rejected. Confirms prior (pre-embargo) result almost exactly - only 15% of instrument-horizon combinations beat Model 1 on RMSE, mean sign agreement change -0.007. Embargo fix barely moved this result, which makes sense: Model 2 has no cross-boundary regression re-fit the way Model 3 does. Time-series momentum/reversion conditioning as designed remains abandoned.
influenced_later_decisions: Confirms Model 3 next, evaluated against Model 1, same ablation methodology.

model_name: Model 3 - Regression/Factor (SPY, Gold, Oil; residual vs Model 1)
notes: Assumes zero expected factor-driven return - forecast is purely the idiosyncratic residual. Mean R2 reported to show how much variance the factors actually explain per instrument. Embargo-adjusted split.
decision: Rejected, more decisively than the pre-embargo result. RMSE win rate DROPPED from 57.4% to 46.3% (now below chance) and mean sign agreement change widened from -0.031 to -0.036 after the embargo fix. Notably, NVDA flipped from beating Model 1 at all 4 horizons (pre-embargo) to losing at all 4 horizons (post-embargo), with sign agreement dropping from 0.593 to 0.430 at h=10 - concrete confirmation that the earlier apparent improvement was inflated by boundary-continuity artifact, exactly what the embargo was built to catch. MSFT remains a genuine, consistent improvement across all horizons (sign agreement 0.515->0.581 at h=10) even after the fix - the one instrument where Model 3 clearly earns its place. Crypto 5d/10d data gap (weekday-only factors vs 7-day crypto trading) remains unresolved.
influenced_later_decisions: Model 3 rejected as a universal addition. MSFT-specific result noted but not enough alone to justify adding regression/factor conditioning system-wide - would need to see if this generalizes to other single-name equities before treating it as more than one instrument look). Proceeding to Model 4.

notes: Probability (logistic regression) and magnitude (stratified trailing mean, same mechanism as Model 1) modeled and combined separately per the blueprint. Point-in-time alignment for classifier training was caught and fixed during development before this ran on real data.
decision: Rejected, decisively - the worst of the four models tested. Only 5% of instrument-horizon combinations beat Model 1 on RMSE (vs 15% for Model 2, 46.3% for Model 3), mean sign agreement change -0.034, and calibration is both poor (mean gap 0.178, worse than Model 1s own ~0.085) and consistently DEGRADES with horizon across nearly every instrument (e.g. GC_F: 0.132->0.396 from h=1 to h=10) - the classifiers probability estimates become progressively less trustworthy at longer horizons, consistent with the same pattern seen in synthetic validation (real injected signal detected well at h=1/h=3, faded by h=10, likely due to fewer independent training episodes within the fixed 400-day window at longer horizons). Some individual results fall notably below chance (QQQ h=10: 0.421). The added complexity of a trained classifier + magnitude submodel does not earn its place over Model 1s simplicity.
influenced_later_decisions: Four consecutive experiments (Models 1-4) have now failed to establish a robust out-of-sample edge on this 15-instrument, 1-10-day-horizon universe using daily data. This is treated as honest evidence, not a process failure - flagged for a checkpoint discussion on next steps before continuing to add model complexity.

model_name: Model 5 - Volatility/Risk (EWMA vs naive rolling window)
notes: Different ablation shape than Models 1-4: tests whether EWMA volatility clustering-aware weighting beats a naive flat rolling window at predicting forward realized volatility, not return direction. h=1 excluded (undefined).
decision: ACCEPTED - the first model to clearly clear the bar. EWMA beats naive rolling-window volatility forecasting on RMSE at 100% of instrument-horizons (45/45), with meaningfully stronger correlation to actual forward volatility (mean 0.300 vs 0.284, and individual instruments up to 0.63 - far higher than any correlation seen in the return-prediction models). Consistent with well-established literature: volatility is far more persistent/forecastable than returns. HG_F shows negative correlation for both estimators (possible genuinely less-persistent copper volatility) but EWMA still wins there too. This becomes the production volatility estimate feeding downstream position sizing, EV-after-risk, and NO-TRADE gating.
influenced_later_decisions: EWMA(lambda=0.94) adopted as the volatility model. Next: ranking engine + NO-TRADE filter, per the direction decision after four rejected return-prediction models.
